newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD, 15 firms to form Japan Internet service firm.
newsitem.headline: KDD, 15 firms to form Japan Internet service firm.

text.p: Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) and 15 other Japanese and foreign companies said on Monday that they would form a company in mid-July to offer connection services for Internet service providers in Japan.

The new company aims to provide commercial-use Internet exchange services. Japan's commercial-use Internet services, currently offered by more than 1,000 Internet service providers, have been connected so far by academic organisations.

The new company, to be called JaPan Internet eXchange, initially hopes to provide connections among about 20 international service providers, KDD said at a news conference held by it and seven of the other companies.

JaPan Internet eXchange will be capitalised at 250 million yen, and KDD will hold a 24 percent stake. Other major shareholders include AT&T Janes, a group company of AT&T Corp , NEC Corp, Fujitsu Ltd, and Sony Systems Design.
KDD said the new company aims for sales of 500 million yen in the year starting on April 1, 1998.
"We want to make this Internet exchange the biggest Internet hub in Asia," said KDD executive Yoshikazu Ikeda.
